Size your trade

Keep the amount at risk small. Start with the 0.5% preset.

Costs & calculation

0.20% is an editable estimate, not your exchange fee. Funding is excluded. Size = risk budget ÷ (stop distance % + costs %). Leverage choices come from the current contract feed. Risk-based size is rounded down to the contract step and capped at 25% account margin and published market-order limits. Delta simulations stay inside the base margin tier. Raising leverage changes required margin and liquidation risk, not the strategy’s technical quality.

How risk-based position sizing works ↗
Enter your balance after selecting a qualifying setup.

One position at a time. Pause after two full-stop losses in a day. Use isolated margin if available. Check contract size and liquidation price before placing an order; gaps and slippage can exceed the planned loss.

2

Backtest this leverage

Test this coin and strategy on the latest available history (up to 1,000 candles per timeframe).

No test run yet. No win probability has been assumed.
What this test means

Tests the same technical rules using only candles closed at each signal. Watches wait for a 1h close beyond the entry trigger, for up to 12 hours. Scalp signals enter at the next 1h open. Middle-of-range EMA setups wait for an edge and are not traded.

Stops use the opposite range edge for EMA setups, one 4h average true range below the trigger for Breakout Watch, or the far side of the signal candle and broken level for scalp setups. Entry uses the next 1h open; gaps over 2% from the reference are skipped. Target is twice the entry-to-stop distance. Exit after 24 hours, or 6 hours for scalp trades. Stop wins if both levels are touched in one candle. No overlapping trades. Open-ended trades and missing history are excluded.

Uses today’s contract limits for historical simulations, not historical leverage schedules. Isolated liquidation is estimated using current maintenance tiers and last-price candles, not historical mark prices. On estimated liquidation, the model charges the full allocated margin plus the configured costs. Cross margin, top-ups, funding and exact liquidation fees are not modeled. Results are estimates. Profitable trades count as wins after the costs above, including timed exits. The current turnover filter, funding, order-book liquidity and news are not replayed. This is a pattern backtest on one coin, not an independently validated probability of your next trade. At least 30 trades are required before showing a percentage; even then, history may not repeat.

Delta connection & fixed IP

For hosted Delta trading, configure a fixed-IP trading server and allowlist its outbound IP once in Delta. Delta requires IP allowlisting for trading keys. If your public IP changes, update the key’s allowlist. Shark can use the connection below; its API permissions depend on your key. No withdrawal route exists in either connection.

Run the local bundle with Node 24 from a trusted computer, then open http://localhost:8787. Connections are saved until you disconnect. Do not paste keys into chat.

Delta account

Connect to see your actual positions, stop orders and fills.

Delta requires Trading permission even to read positions and orders. Allowlist the public IP shown above when running locally; add IPv6 too if Delta reports it. Leave the site’s reviewed order actions box unchecked until you verify the account view. Do not grant withdrawal permission. The hosted site has no fixed outbound IP, so a Delta key requiring an IP allowlist may fail there. Keys are saved encrypted; disconnect removes the saved connection.
